#### Marisol Rubio for San Ramon City Council, District 4
#### PROVEN EXPERIENCE TRANSPARENCY VISION
### That's why San Ramon was ranked #1 for Quality of Life in the Nation!
- Social Progress Map (2025-26)
Donate
### The Best and Clear Choice for San Ramon!
The Only Candidate:
With any public service experience in San Ramon. Four years on the City Council and two years on the DSRSD water district.
Who has lived & raised a child in San Ramon and spent nearly 13 years understanding our residents' current wants and needs.
With proven leadership who has delivered measurable outcomes for San Ramon.
Successfully negotiated the first-ever free childcare in San Ramon for families who need this additional support to work or go to school. This is fully funded by county resources.
Established the first-ever Sustainability Advisory Committee in San Ramon to help implement our Climate Action Plan and proactively address environmental, social, and economic impacts, including but not limited to establishing green corridors and firebreaks, to reduce our carbon footprint and reduce wildfire risks.
Introduced the first display of the Disability Pride Flag to give visibility, public support, and awareness to the needs of people with disabilities.
Addressed State-Mandated Housing requirements through mixed-use, infill development to prevent urban sprawl and protect our parks and open spaces.
Helped launch a free bus service for teens during the summer of 2025 and 2026 - no ID required. Just hop on the bus!
PERSONALLY INITIATED ACHIEVEMENTS
First free childcare in San Ramon for young, working families at no cost to the city.
First Climate Action Task Force that helped update our 2011 Climate Action Plan (CAP) and chartered our first Sustainability Advisory Committee to implement and identify external grants for our CAP. This committee will address city climate sustainability and resiliency issues including minimizing environmental impact, adapting to climate change, meeting present needs without compromising future generations’ ability to meet theirs, surviving climate events, and thriving under changing conditions.
First display of the July Disability Pride Flag to raise awareness about the needs of people with disabilities and be an inclusive society.
Negotiated more inclusionary, affordable workforce housing for our teachers, first responders, essential, and healthcare workers, so that they can work, live, and play in San Ramon.
Expanded residents' access to our community programs by proposing thoughtful, inclusive policies and improving public transportation.
Met state-mandated housing by encouraging balanced mixed use, infill development in the city core to protect our open spaces.
Strengthened our economic profile to attract competitive businesses and tourism through improved community shared spaces and more accessible, safer walk/bike trails including a county-funded Iron Horse Trail dual track system to address safety concerns such as e-bikes. ​
As Director of the Contra Costa County Transportation Agency (CCCTA), we launched the first Youth Ride Free Program in the County and improved Paratransit services for seniors and people with disabilities.
Provided San Ramon high school and college students with internship opportunities through our Teen Government 101 and political leadership opportunities. These are internships my office personally offered and would not be available otherwise.
​​
COUNCIL ACHIEVEMENTS
Traffic Mitigation:
​Constructed an eight award-winning Bollinger Canyon Road Overcrossing that was more than 82% funded by external grants and reduced three hours of red-light traffic onsite daily.
Approved a regional Coordinated Adaptive Ramp Metering (CARM) program on I‑680 at no cost to the city as part of a three‑year demonstration aimed at cutting travel times by about 10%.
Secured $2M in federal funds to advance a fiber-optic network and smart-signal systems that will enhance digital connectivity and transportation efficiency.
Secured additional developer in-lieu impact fees for our city beautification and amenities on the Iron Horse Trail, expanding our library and community services, and maintaining our parks and public works infrastructure.
Maintained a AAA S&P Global financial credit rating and within one year under Measure N resolved an inherited $17.6M structural deficit and attained a general reserve fund surplus.
​
Since assuming office in 2022, San Ramon has consistently improved on every measure of quality of life, public safety, economic growth, transportation, green infrastructure, and financial solvency according to several independent organizations. To ensure that San Ramon continues to be an increasingly safe, vibrant, and innovative model city with a strong economy, we need the continued leadership of experienced, community-engaged, visionary officials who've done the work and proven that they can accomplish what they claim. That’s why Marisol is the only choice for San Ramon, District 4.
Mentored teens over the past four years. Some of my interns were successfully admitted to universities like Northwestern and UC, Berkeley.
Reduced 3 hours of red-Light traffic onsite & secured federal funding to implement fiber-optic Traffic Mitigation Technology.

#### Marisol Rubio for San Ramon City Council, District 4
#### PROVEN EXPERIENCE TRANSPARENCY VISION
### That's why San Ramon was ranked #1 for Quality of Life in the Nation!
- Social Progress Map (2025-26)
Donate
Eighty elected officials, community leaders, and organizations in San Ramon and across Contra Costa County, the Tri-Valley, and the Bay Area support Marisol, because they have seen firsthand her leadership in action and believe in her vision for San Ramon. They know that she has the knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to make San Ramon an innovative, model city, while preserving our small town feel and open spaces. These professional relationships are vital to ensuring that San Ramon receives the attention and resources it needs to thrive and achieve our City's goals.
